response:
FINAL-GENERATION DIAGNOSIS

Gen 8 settled the outstanding design questions and produced the archive's two best signals:

| signal | fmb | alpha | t(α) | Sharpe |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RevenueCheapCapitalReturn (sales-to-price gate) | **5.57** | **3.7%** | **2.76** | 0.13 |
| CheapThreeYearCapitalReturn (MA(3) payload) | 4.29 | 3.5% | 2.47 | **0.24** |
| CheapTotalCapitalDisgorgement (baseline) | 5.43 | 3.5% | 2.62 | 0.24 |
| CheapNetShareholderPayout (shareholder leg only) | 3.85 | 1.5% | 1.07 | −0.02 |

Three conclusions. (1) The **creditor term is indispensable**: dropping Δdebt more than halves the alpha, so the mechanism is capital returned to *all* outside claimants, not net payout to shareholders. (2) **A flow-based cheapness gate works at least as well as the balance-sheet gate**, contradicting my gen-6 prior and showing the mechanism needs low expectations of any credible form, not book-value cheapness specifically. (3) **Three-year averaging preserves alpha while doubling Sharpe**, so the underlying object is a capital-return *policy*, and the single-year measure carries transaction noise.

Each of those was validated in isolation. The final batch therefore (i) combines the two validated single improvements, (ii) tests whether the two cheapness definitions are complements, (iii) repairs the coverage ceiling (0.109) caused by unreported SG&A with a justified missing-data convention, (iv) conditions on the claim-lightness channel that independently produced reliable alpha, and (v) asks structurally whether the shareholder and creditor legs are complements — the one question the ablation raised but could not answer.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: RevenueCheapSustainedCapitalReturn
EXPRESSION: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.6), IND_ZSCORE(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ib, DELTA(ceq, 1)), DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1)), ADD(cogs, xsga)), 2), 3)))
HYPOTHESIS: A firm whose revenue base is discounted by the market while it consistently, over several years, returns capital to shareholders and creditors out of operating surplus is the purest form of the profitable-value configuration: low expectations paired with demonstrated, repeated ability to disgorge cash.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This joins the two improvements that were each validated as isolated single changes in gen 8 — the sales-to-price gate, which produced the archive's best alpha (3.7%) and slope (5.57), and three-year averaging, which produced the best Sharpe (0.24) with alpha intact — and there is no reason for them to interfere since one changes the conditioning set and the other de-noises the payload. It is the natural final specification of the mechanism the archive has converged on.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: DoublyCheapCapitalReturn
EXPRESSION: MUL(MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.6), INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.6)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ib, DELTA(ceq, 1)), DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1)), ADD(cogs, xsga)), 2)))
HYPOTHESIS: A firm cheap on its revenue base but expensive on book assets is asset-light rather than discounted, and one cheap on book but expensive on revenue is asset-heavy rather than discounted; only firms cheap on both measures face genuinely low expectations, and there the evidence of capital return is most informative.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The two gates delivered nearly identical results separately (alpha 3.5% and 3.7%), which raises the question of whether they select the same firms or complementary ones — their intersection answers it, and if the effect strengthens, the mechanism is about unambiguous low expectations rather than any particular multiple. The conjunction is a genuine economic condition, not a threshold tweak, and it keeps roughly a quarter of the cross-section scored, so the extreme portfolios remain populated.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: CapitalReturnFullSampleDeflator
EXPRESSION: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.6), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ib, DELTA(ceq, 1)), DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1)), ADD(cogs, COALESCE(xsga, 0))), 2)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms that do not report selling and administrative expense separately have embedded those costs in cost of goods sold, so treating unreported SG&A as zero measures their operating cost base correctly rather than discarding them; the capital-return mechanism should hold for those firms exactly as it does for separate reporters.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Every signal in this family is capped at coverage 0.109 purely because xsga is missing for a substantial minority of firm-years, and that missingness is a disclosure choice rather than an economic state — the standard justified use of COALESCE. If alpha and slope survive at materially higher coverage, the result is far more credible than one estimated on the subsample that happens to break out overheads, which is the single most important robustness question left.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: UnencumberedCheapCapitalReturn
EXPRESSION: MUL(MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.6), INDICATOR(IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(dp, xint), sale))), 0.5)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ib, DELTA(ceq, 1)), DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1)), ADD(cogs, xsga)), 2)))
HYPOTHESIS: Capital returned by a firm whose revenue is already heavily committed to capital replacement and interest is a transfer out of a shrinking base and cannot be sustained, whereas the same capital return from a lightly encumbered revenue base reflects true surplus that will recur.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The claim-lightness channel independently produced reliable alpha (2.5%, t 2.18, Sharpe 0.13) but a weak slope, and the capital-return flow produced the strongest slopes; entering the former as a *condition* rather than averaging its rank into the payload avoids the dilution that sank both earlier SUMRANK fusions (alpha 1.3% and 0.9%). It tests whether sustainability of the disgorgement is what the market misprices.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: BothClaimantsPaidCheap
EXPRESSION: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.6), IND_ZSCORE(MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, DELTA(ceq, 1)), ADD(cogs, xsga))), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), ADD(cogs, xsga)))))))
HYPOTHESIS: Returning cash to shareholders while simultaneously borrowing more, or repaying debt while issuing equity, are financing rotations rather than evidence of surplus; only a firm paying down both claims at once is genuinely generating more cash than its business requires, and that is the configuration a discounted price contradicts.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The gen-8 ablation showed the shareholder leg alone is weak (alpha 1.5%) while the sum is strong (3.5%), which is consistent with either additivity or complementarity; the weakest-link conjunction distinguishes them, because it scores highly only when both legs are individually high and is not reproducible by their sum. This is the structural question the decomposition raised and is the last one the archive can answer.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: RichFirmsAbsorbingCapital
EXPRESSION: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), 0.6), IND_ZSCORE(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ib, DELTA(ceq, 1)), DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1)), ADD(cogs, xsga)), 2), 3)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms whose revenue commands a high price are valued on expected future profit, and among them the ones that have persistently absorbed outside capital rather than returned it are financing the promised growth from investors; their multiples are the least defensible and their returns the lowest.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The archive has located the level-based claim mechanism on both sides of the valuation distribution (glamour mirror alpha −2.4%, t −3.22) but has never tested the capital-return *flow* in the expensive state using the three-year policy measure, so this determines whether the final mechanism is a two-sided expectation-error effect or a value-side-only one. A reliable negative alpha here would materially strengthen the economic interpretation of the entire family, since it would show the same fundamental discriminates in both expectation regimes.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---CRITIQUE RevenueCheapSustainedCapitalReturn---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: A defensible but purely mechanical merge of two already-tested gen-8 variants whose parents perform almost identically, so the incremental information is small, and the payload — (ib − Δceq − Δdebt), i.e. net distributions to all claimants — remains a close relative of the published net-external-financing/total-payout anomaly conditioned on value, which limits novelty even if the test is worth one run.

---CRITIQUE DoublyCheapCapitalReturn---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Intersecting two highly correlated market-cap-scaled cheapness gates is a conditioning/threshold tweak rather than a new economic mechanism, and because sales/P and B/P share the same denominator the intersection will largely reproduce either parent while further thinning an already coverage-constrained (0.109) sample.

---CRITIQUE CapitalReturnFullSampleDeflator---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: This is a data-handling robustness check on the deflator, not a cross-theme signal; the coverage gain over the parent is modest (~0.109 → ~0.14 at best), and COALESCE(xsga,0) silently changes the deflator's economic meaning across reporting regimes, so a "surviving" result is as likely to reflect deflator heterogeneity as genuine breadth.

---CRITIQUE UnencumberedCheapCapitalReturn---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The sustainability condition is economically coherent and gating rather than rank-averaging is the right response to the earlier SUMRANK dilution, but stacking a second 0.5 gate on top of a 0.6 gate within an already sparse sample risks unstable extreme portfolios, so coverage and turnover diagnostics must be checked before crediting any alpha improvement.

---CRITIQUE BothClaimantsPaidCheap---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: This is the one proposal that asks a genuine structural question — whether the shareholder-payout and debt-retirement legs are additive or complementary — and the MIN construction is not reproducible by the existing sum, so the result is informative regardless of sign; it is distinct from the earlier CheapCashBackedCapitalReturn, which paired the combined flow with operating cash flow instead.

---CRITIQUE RichFirmsAbsorbingCapital---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The stated sign contradicts the expression: the payload is high when a firm *returns* capital and low when it *absorbs* it, so the hypothesis ("capital absorbers underperform") implies a positive slope, not the declared negative one, and beyond this inconsistency the design is a sign-flipped gate on an already-tested payload.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: ProfitableCheapCapitalReturn
EXPRESSION: MUL(MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.6), INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, sale)), 0.5)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ib, DELTA(ceq, 1)), DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1)), ADD(cogs, xsga)), 2)))
HYPOTHESIS: Capital handed back by a business that earns an above-median operating margin is surplus generated by trade, whereas the same capital returned by a sub-margin business is proceeds of shrinkage — asset sales, inventory run-down, or under-investment — so profitability determines whether disgorgement by a cheap firm is evidence of hidden strength or of managed decline.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This replaces the intersection of two collinear price-scaled gates with a condition drawn from the other theme entirely — operating margin — restoring an explicit profitability leg to a family that has drifted toward pure financing flows, and it is exactly the discrimination the archive's leading signal cannot make. The margin screen at the industry median leaves roughly 30% of firms scored, comparable to the accepted claim-lightness variant, so portfolio breadth is preserved.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: LeveredRevenueCheapSustainedReturn
EXPRESSION: MUL(MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.6), INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at)), 0.5)), IND_ZSCORE(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ib, DELTA(ceq, 1)), DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1)), ADD(cogs, xsga)), 2), 3)))
HYPOTHESIS: Where the equity of a discounted firm is effectively a residual option on the enterprise, a sustained multi-year policy of returning capital to shareholders and creditors shifts proportionally more value to equity than the same policy at an unlevered firm, because each dollar of claim extinguished raises the probability that the equity finishes in the money.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This abandons the data-handling check for a consolidation of three separately validated elements — the sales-to-price gate (alpha 3.7%, fmb 5.57), the leverage condition that was accepted as a genuine economic amplifier (alpha 3.5%, fmb 4.94), and three-year averaging (Sharpe 0.24) — each of which was tested in isolation so the combination is interpretable rather than exploratory. The leverage screen is the one condition with a mechanism explaining *why* the effect should be larger rather than merely where it is measured.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: TwoSidedCapitalReturnExpectations
EXPRESSION: MUL(SUB(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.6), INDICATOR(IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), 0.6)), IND_ZSCORE(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ib, DELTA(ceq, 1)), DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1)), ADD(cogs, xsga)), 2), 3)))
HYPOTHESIS: The mispricing is the disagreement between what price implies and what capital flows reveal: cheap firms that persistently return capital are stronger than their price admits, and expensive firms that persistently absorb outside capital are weaker than their price assumes, so the two corners belong in the same signal with opposite weights.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: The state variable takes the values +1, 0 and −1 across the cheap, middle and expensive thirds and multiplies the capital-return z-score, so the score is highest for cheap disgorgers and lowest for expensive absorbers — which fixes the sign inconsistency of the previous version and, more importantly, makes the construction a true interaction term rather than a gated single-state effect. It is the one specification that tests the project's central claim directly, that profitability-type evidence flips its return implication with the valuation state instead of merely being layered onto it.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
